Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 70, verses 1–5:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall, for the disbelievers, which none can avert, from God, Lord of the ascending stairways. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years. So be patient with a beautiful patience.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The reciters differed over the reading of His saying: ﴿saala sa'il﴾. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it ﴿sa'ala sa'il﴾ with a hamza on sa'ala, meaning: a questioner among the disbelievers asked about the punishment of God, by whom it would fall. Some of the reciters of Madina read it ﴿sala sa'il﴾ without a hamza on sa'ala, and they took it to be a verb derived from "sail" (flood, torrent).

The reading that is more correct of the two is the reading of the one who reads it with the hamza, because the reciters are agreed upon it (ijma' al-hujja min al-qurra'), and because most of the early interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil min al-salaf) interpreted it in the sense of the hamza.

Mention of those who interpreted it in this way, and said its interpretation is similar to what we have said about it:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾: He said: That is the asking of the disbelievers about the punishment of God, and it is befalling.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿If this is indeed the truth from You...﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿A questioner asked﴾, he said: One who calls out called out, ﴿about a punishment that is to befall﴾, he said: It will befall in the Hereafter. He said: And it is their saying: ﴿O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾, he said: Peoples asked for the punishment of God, so God made clear upon whom it would fall: upon the disbelievers.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked﴾, he said: He asked about a punishment that is to befall, so God said: ﴿for the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾.

As for those who read it without a hamza, they said: "al-sa'il" is a valley from the valleys of Hell.

Mention of those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾: Some people of knowledge said: It is a valley in Hell called Sa'il.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿about a punishment that is to befall, for the disbelievers﴾,

it means: he asked about a punishment for the disbelievers, which is binding upon them on the Day of Resurrection and will befall them. The meaning of ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ is "upon the disbelievers," as was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿about a punishment that is to befall, for the disbelievers﴾: It is befalling upon the disbelievers. The preposition (al-lam) in His saying ﴿lil-kafirin﴾ is attached to the word "befalling" (al-waqi').

* *

As for His saying: ﴿which none can avert, from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾,

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, means: there is no one who can avert from the disbelievers, from God, the punishment that befalls them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾,

it means: Lord of height, of degrees, of bounties and favours.

The people of interpretation said what is similar to what we have said about it.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: He means height and bounties.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾: Lord of bounties and favours.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: The stairways of the heaven.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: God is the Lord of the ascending stairways.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: Lord of the degrees.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾,

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, means: the angels and the Spirit, who is Gabriel, peace be upon him, ascend to Him, meaning to God, may He be majestic and exalted. The pronoun in His saying ﴿to Him﴾ refers to the name of God. ﴿In a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ means: the measure of their ascent in that Day, for others among creation, is fifty thousand years. That is because they ascend from the furthest point of His command, from beneath the seventh earth, to the furthest point of His command, above the seven heavens.

The people of interpretation said what is similar to what we have said about it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Ma'ruf, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: The furthest point of His command, from beneath the earths, to the furthest point of His command, above the heavens, is a measure of fifty thousand years; and a day whose measure is a thousand years, meaning by that the descent of the command from the sky to the earth and from the earth to the sky in one day, so that is its measure of a thousand years, because the distance between the sky and the earth is a five-hundred-year journey.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day in which He finishes judging between His creatures, and the measure of that Day in which He finished judging between them was fifty thousand years.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrima, regarding ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: In one day, in which He finishes the judgment, like the measure of fifty thousand years.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrima, regarding ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: The Day of Resurrection.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrima, regarding this verse, ﴿fifty thousand years﴾: The Day of Resurrection.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: That is the Day of Resurrection.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, Ma'mar said: It has also reached me from 'Ikrima, regarding His saying: ﴿whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: No one knows how much has passed, nor how much remains, except God.

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: This is the Day of Resurrection, which God made, for the disbelievers, a measure of fifty thousand years.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: meaning the Day of Resurrection.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: This is the Day of Resurrection.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Darraj narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id, that he said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ — how long is this? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer which he prays in this world."

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this, a view other than the one we have mentioned from him, namely what follows:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, that a man asked Ibn 'Abbas about a day whose measure is a thousand years. He said: What of a day whose measure is fifty thousand years? The man said: I only asked you so that you would inform me. He said: They are two days which God mentioned in the Qur'an; God knows best about them, and he disliked to say in the Book of God what he did not know.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: A man asked Ibn 'Abbas about a day whose measure is a thousand years. He said: He doubted him, and it was mentioned to him concerning it, so he said: What of a day whose measure is fifty thousand years? The man said: I only asked you so that you would inform me. He said: They are two days which God, may He be majestic and exalted, mentioned; God knows best about them, and I dislike to say in the Book of God what I do not know.

The recitation of the majority of the reciters of the regions was ﴿ta'ruju al-mala'ikatu wal-ruh﴾ with a "ta" (feminine verbal prefix), except al-Kisa'i, who read it with a "ya", on the authority of a report he transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud that he read it so.

The correct recitation, in our view, is what the reciters of the regions read, namely with the "ta", because the reciters are agreed upon it (ijma' al-hujja).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾,

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, means: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾, that is, patience without complaint. He says to him: Be patient with the harm these polytheists inflict upon you, and let not the adversity you meet from them turn you away from conveying the message that your Lord has commanded you to convey to them.

Ibn Zayd used to say regarding this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾: This was when he was commanded to pardon them and not to requite them. Then, when he was commanded to fight and to be harsh with them, he was commanded to be severe and to kill until they desisted, and this abrogated that. Mention of those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾: Some people of knowledge said: It is a valley in Hell called Sa'il.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿about a punishment that is to befall, for the disbelievers﴾,

it means: he asked about a punishment for the disbelievers, which is binding upon them on the Day of Resurrection and will befall them. The meaning of ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ is "upon the disbelievers," as was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿about a punishment that is to befall, for the disbelievers﴾: It is befalling upon the disbelievers. The preposition (al-lam) in His saying ﴿lil-kafirin﴾ is attached to the word "befalling" (al-waqi').

* *

As for His saying: ﴿which none can avert, from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾,

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, means: there is no one who can avert from the disbelievers, from God, the punishment that befalls them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾,

it means: Lord of height, of degrees, of bounties and favours.

The people of interpretation said what is similar to what we have said about it.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: He means height and bounties.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾: Lord of bounties and favours.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: The stairways of the heaven.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: God is the Lord of the ascending stairways.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, he said: Lord of the degrees.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾,

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, means: the angels and the Spirit, who is Gabriel, peace be upon him, ascend to Him, meaning to God, may He be majestic and exalted. The pronoun in His saying ﴿to Him﴾ refers to the name of God. ﴿In a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ means: the measure of their ascent in that Day, for others among creation, is fifty thousand years. That is because they ascend from the furthest point of His command, from beneath the seventh earth, to the furthest point of His command, above the seven heavens.

The people of interpretation said what is similar to what we have said about it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Ma'ruf, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: The furthest point of His command, from beneath the earths, to the furthest point of His command, above the heavens, is a measure of fifty thousand years; and a day whose measure is a thousand years, meaning by that the descent of the command from the sky to the earth and from the earth to the sky in one day, so that is its measure of a thousand years, because the distance between the sky and the earth is a five-hundred-year journey.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day in which He finishes judging between His creatures, and the measure of that Day in which He finished judging between them was fifty thousand years.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrima, regarding ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: In one day, in which He finishes the judgment, like the measure of fifty thousand years.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrima, regarding ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: The Day of Resurrection.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrima, regarding this verse, ﴿fifty thousand years﴾: The Day of Resurrection.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: That is the Day of Resurrection.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, Ma'mar said: It has also reached me from 'Ikrima, regarding His saying: ﴿whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: No one knows how much has passed, nor how much remains, except God.

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: This is the Day of Resurrection, which God made, for the disbelievers, a measure of fifty thousand years.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: meaning the Day of Resurrection.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾: This is the Day of Resurrection.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Darraj narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id, that he said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ — how long is this? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer which he prays in this world."

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this, a view other than the one we have mentioned from him, namely what follows:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, that a man asked Ibn 'Abbas about a day whose measure is a thousand years. He said: What of a day whose measure is fifty thousand years? The man said: I only asked you so that you would inform me. He said: They are two days which God mentioned in the Qur'an; God knows best about them, and he disliked to say in the Book of God what he did not know.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: A man asked Ibn 'Abbas about a day whose measure is a thousand years. He said: He doubted him, and it was mentioned to him concerning it, so he said: What of a day whose measure is fifty thousand years? The man said: I only asked you so that you would inform me. He said: They are two days which God, may He be majestic and exalted, mentioned; God knows best about them, and I dislike to say in the Book of God what I do not know.

The recitation of the majority of the reciters of the regions was ﴿ta'ruju al-mala'ikatu wal-ruh﴾ with a "ta" (feminine verbal prefix), except al-Kisa'i, who read it with a "ya", on the authority of a report he transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud that he read it so.

The correct recitation, in our view, is what the reciters of the regions read, namely with the "ta", because the reciters are agreed upon it (ijma' al-hujja).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾,

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, means: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾, that is, patience without complaint. He says to him: Be patient with the harm these polytheists inflict upon you, and let not the adversity you meet from them turn you away from conveying the message that your Lord has commanded you to convey to them.

Ibn Zayd used to say regarding this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So be patient with a beautiful patience﴾: This was when he was commanded to pardon them and not to requite them. Then, when he was commanded to fight and to be harsh with them, he was commanded to be severe and to kill until they desisted, and this abrogated that. What Ibn Zayd said, that he had been commanded to pardon by this verse and then that was abrogated, is a claim without any basis, because there is no indication for the soundness of what he said by any of the means by which claims are validated. And in God's command to His Prophet (ﷺ) concerning beautiful patience over the harm of the polytheists there is nothing that requires that it be a command from Him to him only in some circumstances; rather, it was a command from God to him in all circumstances, because he (ﷺ) never ceased, from the time God sent him until He took him, to suffer harm from them, and in all of that he was patient over what he met from them of harm, both before God permitted him to fight them and after He permitted him to do so.

The interpretation of His saying, [Exalted is He]: ﴿Indeed, they see it as distant (6) but We see it as near (7) on the day the sky will be like molten brass (8) and the mountains like wool (9), and no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend (10) though they will be made to see them.﴾

His saying, [Exalted is His remembrance]: Indeed, these polytheists see the punishment about which they asked, which will befall them, as distant in its occurrence. God, exalted is His praise, only informed that they see it as distant because they did not believe in it and denied resurrection after death, and reward and punishment. So He said: they see it as not occurring, while We see it as near, because it is certain to happen, and everything that is coming is near.

The "hāʾ" and "mīm" in His saying ﴿Indeed, they (innahum)﴾ refer to the disbelievers, and the "hāʾ" in His saying ﴿they see it (yarawnahu)﴾ refers to the punishment.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿on the day the sky will be like molten brass (al-muhl)﴾

His saying, [Exalted is His remembrance]: On the day the sky will be like a melted substance. I have already explained the meaning of al-muhl earlier, with its evidences and the disagreement of those who differed about it, and I mentioned what the early scholars (al-salaf) said about it, so that is sufficient and there is no need to repeat it in this place.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿on the day the sky will be like molten brass﴾, he said: "Like the dregs of olive oil."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿on the day the sky will be like molten brass﴾: it will change on that day to another color, toward redness.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the mountains will be like wool (al-ʿihn)﴾

He says: and the mountains will be like wool.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿like wool (al-ʿihn)﴾, he said: "Like wool."

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿like wool﴾, he said: "Like wool."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend, though they will be made to see them﴾

His saying, [Exalted is His remembrance]: And no close relative will ask his close relative about his condition, because he is occupied with his own condition.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend﴾: each person is occupied with himself, away from people.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿though they will be made to see them (yubaṣṣarunahum)﴾

The people of interpretation differed about who is meant by the "hāʾ" and "mīm" in His saying ﴿they will be made to see them (yubaṣṣarunahum)﴾. Some of them said: it refers to relatives, that they recognize their relatives, and each person recognizes his close relative; this is God's making them see one another.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿they will be made to see them﴾, he said: some of them recognize others, and they recognize one another, then some of them flee from others, saying: ﴿For every one of them, that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿they will be made to see them﴾: they recognize them, they know them; by God, people will recognize people and folk will recognize folk.

Others said: rather, it refers to the believers, that they see the disbelievers.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿they will be made to see them﴾: the believers see the disbelievers.

Others said: rather, it refers to the disbelievers who had been followers of others in disbelief in the world, that they recognize their leaders in the Fire.

Those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿they will be made to see them﴾: they see those who misled them in the world, in the Fire.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: no intimate friend will ask another intimate friend about his condition, but they will be made to see them and will recognize them, then some of them will flee from others, as the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his spouse and his children. For every one of them, that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾.

We only said that this is the most correct interpretation because it best matches what the apparent wording of the revelation indicates, namely that His saying ﴿they will be made to see them﴾ follows His saying ﴿and no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend﴾, so it is more fitting that the "hāʾ" and "mīm" refer to them than to others.

The reciters differed in reading His saying ﴿and no one will ask (wa-lā yus'alu)﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional centers (qurrāʾ al-amṣār), other than Abu Jaʿfar al-Qari and Shayba, read it with a fatha on the yāʾ (yas'alu). Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read ﴿wa-lā yus'alu﴾ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, meaning: it is not said to an intimate friend, "Where is your intimate friend?", and they do not ask one another.

The correct reading in our view is the fatha on the yāʾ, meaning: people do not ask one another about their condition, because this meaning is sound and because the consensus of the authoritative reciters (ijmaʿ al-ḥujja min al-qurrāʾ) is upon it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 70, verses 11–18**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿The guilty one would wish he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his sons, (11) and his wife and his brother, (12) and his kin who shelter him, (13) and all who are on earth, then it would deliver him. (14)﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: The disbeliever, on that Day, wishes and longs that he could ransom himself from God's punishment of him on that Day with his sons, and his wife (the *sahibah* is his spouse), and his brother, and his *fasilah*, who are his clan that shelters him, meaning those who take him into their household and whose wife lodges with him, because of the nearness between her and him, and with all who are on earth of creation, and then that would deliver him from God's punishment of him on that Day. God, exalted is His praise, began with mentioning the sons, then the spouse, then the brother, informing His servants that the disbeliever, because of the great calamity that will befall him on that Day, would ransom himself, if he found a way to do so, with the people most beloved to him when he was in this world, and those nearest to him in lineage.

Those of the people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿The guilty one would wish he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his sons, and his wife and his brother, and his kin who shelter him﴾: the most beloved and then the nearest, from among his family and clan, because of the severities of that Day.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and his kin who shelter him﴾: he said, "His tribe."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and his wife﴾, he said: "The *sahibah* is the wife." ﴿and his kin who shelter him﴾, he said: "His *fasilah* is his clan."

* * *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed it is the Blaze, (15) plucking out the scalp, (16) calling those who turned their backs and withdrew, (17) and gathered and hoarded. (18)﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: No, it is not as they think; nothing will deliver him from God's punishment. Then He began to inform of what He has prepared for him there, exalted is His praise, saying: ﴿Indeed it is the Blaze﴾. *Laza* (Blaze) is one of the names of Hell, and for this reason it is not declined.

The grammarians differed regarding its grammatical position (*i'rab*). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its position is in the accusative as an apposition (*badal*) to the pronoun *ha'* (in *innaha*), and the predicate of *inna* is ﴿plucking out﴾ (*nazza'ah*). He said: If you wish, you may make *laza* nominative as the predicate of *inna*, and make *nazza'ah* nominative as the subject (*mubtada'*). Some who rejected this said: The explicit noun should not follow the pronominal (suffixed) form except in rare usage. He said: The preferred reading is ﴿Indeed it is the Blaze, plucking out the scalp﴾ with *laza* as the predicate and *nazza'ah* as a circumstantial state (*hal*). He said: Whoever makes it nominative begins a new sentence, because it is either praise or blame, and it cannot be a subject (*ibtida'*) except in that way.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that *laza* is the predicate and *nazza'ah* is the subject, so it is nominative. The accusative is not permitted in recitation, because the readers of the major cities (*qurra' al-amsar*) agree on its being nominative, and no reader has recited it in the accusative. Although the accusative has a valid basis in Arabic, it is also permissible that the *ha'* in His words *innaha* be a separating pronoun (*'imad*), with *laza* nominative as the subject of *nazza'ah*, and *nazza'ah* with *laza*, as one says: *innaha Hind qa'imah* and *innahu Hind qa'imah*, with the *ha'* being a separating pronoun in both cases.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾:

God, exalted is His remembrance, says, informing about *Laza*: indeed it plucks out the skin of the head and the extremities of the body. *Al-Shawa* is the plural of *shawah*, and it refers to the limbs of a human being other than the vital parts. It is said: "He shot and missed (*fa-ashwa*)" when he did not hit a vital spot. Sometimes a describer applies the term to the skin of the head, as al-A'sha said:

*Qalat Qutaylah ma lahu qad jullilat shayban shawatuh*
(Qutaylah said: "What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with white hair.")

[The verse is in the Diwan of al-A'sha (Vienna edition, p. 238), though the editor notes it is attributed to him and is not in his Diwan. It is one of the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah (in Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 180), who said: "*al-Shawa*: its singular is *shawah*, and it is the two hands, the two feet and the head of human beings." Al-A'sha: "Qalat Qutaylah..." the verse. In (Lisan, root sh-w-y), al-Farra' said regarding His words (*kalla innaha laza nazza'ah lil-shawa*): "*al-Shawa*: the two hands, the two feet, the tips of the fingers, and the skull of the head. The skin of the head is called *shawah*." Al-Zajjaj said: "*al-Shawa*: the plural of *al-shawah*, which is the skin of the head," and he recited: "Qalat Qutaylah ma lahu..." the verse.]

And sometimes it is used to describe the shank, as in their description of a horse:

*'Abl al-shawa nahd al-juzarah*
(thick-limbed, with a high-raised chest and a long neck)

[This is the second half of a verse by al-A'sha of Bani Qays ibn Tha'labah, from a poem in the *mujazz* meter satirizing Shayban ibn Shihab al-Jahduri, whose opening is: "O my neighbour, you were not a neighbour." (His Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 153 and following.) Here is the verse with the witness in full, together with two verses before it (from *Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra* 1:83):
"And there your assumption will prove false... that there would be no gathering nor visit,
nor will the innocent be granted innocence, nor gift, nor protection,
except a ride, or a horse, swift, thick-limbed (*nahd al-juzarah*)."
Al-Baghdadi said: He says: when we attack you, you will know that your assumption that we will not attack you is false; your claim is that we will neither gather nor visit you with horses and weapons as raiders against you. Whoever among you is innocent will not benefit from his innocence, because when war becomes severe its evil reaches the innocent as it reaches the guilty; and we will not accept gifts from you, nor give you protection by which you may be safe from us. *Khifarah* (protection), with a *damma* or *kasra*, means covenant. *Illa 'ulalah*: that is, but we will visit you on horses. *Al-'Ulalah* is the remainder of the horse's run from *al-ta'allul*, meaning amusement. *Al-Badahah* is the horse's first run. *Al-Sabih* is the horse that scrapes the earth with its forelegs in running. *Al-nahd* is the raised one. *Al-juzarah* is the head, the two hands and the two feet. He means that in its neck and legs there is length and height, for it is preferred in horses to have a long, supple neck. It is also preferred that what is above the two shanks, the thighs, be long, and then it is described as having long legs. End. The half-verse cited by the author as a witness differs from al-A'sha's half-verse, but the point of the witness is in it. End.]

He means by that: its legs. The root of all this is what I have described.

Those of the people of *ta'wil* said the same as what we have said about this.

* Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt related to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah related to us, from Qabus, from his father, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, and he said: "It plucks out the crown of the head."

* Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sawwaf related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Muhalhil Abu Kudaynah related to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, he said: "It plucks out the head."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾: "It means the skins and the skulls."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, he said: "It plucks the skins of the head."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, and he did not inform me, so I asked Mujahid about it, and I said: "The flesh apart from the bone?" He said: "Yes."

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, he said: "The flesh of the shank."

* Muhammad ibn 'Umarah al-Asadi related to me, saying: Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah al-Suwa'i related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, he said: "It plucks the flesh of the two shanks."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Qurrah ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾, he said: "It burns the head, consuming everything of it, while its heart remains cooked."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 70, verses 11–18**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿The guilty one would wish he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his sons, (11) and his wife and his brother, (12) and his kin who shelter him, (13) and all who are on earth, then it would deliver him. (14)﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: The disbeliever, on that Day, wishes and longs that he could ransom himself from God's punishment of him on that Day with his sons, and his wife (the *sahibah* is his spouse), and his brother, and his *fasilah*, who are his clan that shelters him, meaning those who take him into their household and whose wife lodges with him, because of the nearness between her and him, and with all who are on earth of creation, and then that would deliver him from God's punishment of him on that Day. God, exalted is His praise, began with mentioning the sons, then the spouse, then the brother, informing His servants that the disbeliever, because of the great calamity that will befall him on that Day, would ransom himself, if he found a way to do so, with the people most beloved to him when he was in this world, and those nearest to him in lineage.

Those of the people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿The guilty one would wish he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his sons, and his wife and his brother, and his kin who shelter him﴾: the most beloved and then the nearest, from among his family and clan, because of the severities of that Day.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and his kin who shelter him﴾: he said, "His tribe."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and his wife﴾, he said: "The *sahibah* is the wife." ﴿and his kin who shelter him﴾, he said: "His *fasilah* is his clan."

* * *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed it is the Blaze, (15) plucking out the scalp, (16) calling those who turned their backs and withdrew, (17) and gathered and hoarded. (18)﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: No, it is not as they think; nothing will deliver him from God's punishment. Then He began to inform of what He has prepared for him there, exalted is His praise, saying: ﴿Indeed it is the Blaze﴾. *Laza* (Blaze) is one of the names of Hell, and for this reason it is not declined.

The grammarians differed regarding its grammatical position (*i'rab*). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its position is in the accusative as an apposition (*badal*) to the pronoun *ha'* (in *innaha*), and the predicate of *inna* is ﴿plucking out﴾ (*nazza'ah*). He said: If you wish, you may make *laza* nominative as the predicate of *inna*, and make *nazza'ah* nominative as the subject (*mubtada'*). Some who rejected this said: The explicit noun should not follow the pronominal (suffixed) form except in rare usage. He said: The preferred reading is ﴿Indeed it is the Blaze, plucking out the scalp﴾ with *laza* as the predicate and *nazza'ah* as a circumstantial state (*hal*). He said: Whoever makes it nominative begins a new sentence, because it is either praise or blame, and it cannot be a subject (*ibtida'*) except in that way.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that *laza* is the predicate and *nazza'ah* is the subject, so it is nominative. The accusative is not permitted in recitation, because the readers of the major cities (*qurra' al-amsar*) agree on its being nominative, and no reader has recited it in the accusative. Although the accusative has a valid basis in Arabic, it is also permissible that the *ha'* in His words *innaha* be a separating pronoun (*'imad*), with *laza* nominative as the subject of *nazza'ah*, and *nazza'ah* with *laza*, as one says: *innaha Hind qa'imah* and *innahu Hind qa'imah*, with the *ha'* being a separating pronoun in both cases.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿plucking out the scalp﴾:

God, exalted is His remembrance, says, informing about *Laza*: indeed it plucks out the skin of the head and the extremities of the body. *Al-Shawa* is the plural of *shawah*, and it refers to the limbs of a human being other than the vital parts. It is said: "He shot and missed (*fa-ashwa*)" when he did not hit a vital spot. Sometimes a describer applies the term to the skin of the head, as al-A'sha said:

*Qalat Qutaylah ma lahu qad jullilat shayban shawatuh*
(Qutaylah said: "What is wrong with him? His scalp has been covered with white hair.")

[The verse is in the Diwan of al-A'sha (Vienna edition, p. 238), though the editor notes it is attributed to him and is not in his Diwan. It is one of the witnesses of Abu 'Ubaydah (in Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 180), who said: "*al-Shawa*: its singular is *shawah*, and it is the two hands, the two feet and the head of human beings." Al-A'sha: "Qalat Qutaylah..." the verse. In (Lisan, root sh-w-y), al-Farra' said regarding His words (*kalla innaha laza nazza'ah lil-shawa*): "*al-Shawa*: the two hands, the two feet, the tips of the fingers, and the skull of the head. The skin of the head is called *shawah*." Al-Zajjaj said: "*al-Shawa*: the plural of *al-shawah*, which is the skin of the head," and he recited: "Qalat Qutaylah ma lahu..." the verse.]

And sometimes it is used to describe the shank, as in their description of a horse:

*'Abl al-shawa nahd al-juzarah*
(thick-limbed, with a high-raised chest and a long neck)

[This is the second half of a verse by al-A'sha of Bani Qays ibn Tha'labah, from a poem in the *mujazz* meter satirizing Shayban ibn Shihab al-Jahduri, whose opening is: "O my neighbour, you were not a neighbour." (His Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 153 and following.) Here is the verse with the witness in full, together with two verses before it (from *Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra* 1:83):
"And there your assumption will prove false... that there would be no gathering nor visit,
nor will the innocent be granted innocence, nor gift, nor protection,
except a ride, or a horse, swift, thick-limbed (*nahd al-juzarah*)."
Al-Baghdadi said: He says: when we attack you, you will know that your assumption that we will not attack you is false; your claim is that we will neither gather nor visit you with horses and weapons as raiders against you. Whoever among you is innocent will not benefit from his innocence, because when war becomes severe its evil reaches the innocent as it reaches the guilty; and we will not accept gifts from you, nor give you protection by which you may be safe from us. *Khifarah* (protection), with a *damma* or *kasra*, means covenant. *Illa 'ulalah*: that is, but we will visit you on horses. *Al-'Ulalah* is the remainder of the horse's run from *al-ta'allul*, meaning amusement. *Al-Badahah* is the horse's first run. *Al-Sabih* is the horse that scrapes the earth with its forelegs in running. *Al-nahd* is the raised one. *Al-juzarah* is the head, the two hands and the two feet. He means that in its neck and legs there is length and height, for it is preferred in horses to have a long, supple neck. It is also preferred that what is above the two shanks, the thighs, be long, and then it is described as having long legs. End. The half-verse cited by the author as a witness differs from al-A'sha's half-verse, but the point of the witness is in it. End.]

He means by that: its legs. The root of all this is what I have described.

Tafsir of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 70, verses 19–23:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious (hal'an).(19) When evil touches him, he is distressed (jazu'an).(20) And when good touches him, he withholds (mana'an).(21) Except the observers of prayer (al-musallin),(22) Those who are constant in their prayer,(23)﴾

His saying, the Exalted, means: ﴿Indeed, mankind﴾ the disbeliever ﴿was created anxious﴾. Al-halu' (هلع, anxiety): intense distress together with intense greed and impatience.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾. He said: it is the one about whom Allah said ﴿when evil touches him, he is distressed, and when good touches him, he withholds﴾. It is said: al-Halu' is the one who is very distressed and greedy, and this is about the people of polytheism.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Ishaq, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾. He said: miserly and distressed.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Ikrima: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾. He said: impatient.

I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿Indeed, mankind﴾ meaning the disbeliever, ﴿was created anxious﴾, meaning: he is stingy, withholding good, distressed when calamity befalls him. This is the anxious (al-halu').

Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi narrated to us, he said: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Husayn, Yahya said, Khalid said: I asked Shu'ba about His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾, and Shu'ba narrated to me from Husayn that he said: al-Halu': the greedy.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, he said: I asked Husayn about this verse: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾, and he said: greedy.

Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾: al-Halu': the distressed.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿was created anxious﴾: distressed.

And His saying: ﴿When evil touches him, he is distressed﴾

He means: when his wealth decreases and poverty and destitution reach him, he is distressed by that, having no patience with it. ﴿And when good touches him, he withholds﴾ means: and when his wealth increases and he attains riches, he withholds what is in his hand, miserly with it, not spending it in obedience to Allah, nor paying the right of Allah from it.

And His saying: ﴿Except the observers of prayer, those who are constant in their prayer﴾

He means: except those who obey Allah by performing the prayer He has enjoined upon them, and who maintain it without neglecting any part of it. Such people are not among those created anxious, while the (anxious person) is, along with that, a disbeliever in his Lord who does not pray to Allah.

It has been said: by His saying ﴿except the observers of prayer﴾ is meant the believers who were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has also been said: it refers to everyone who prays the five (obligatory prayers).

Zurayq ibn al-Sakhab narrated to me, he said: Mu'awiya ibn 'Amr narrated to us, he said: Za'ida narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿those who are constant in their prayer﴾. He said: the five prayers.

In the interpretation of His words, "Except those who have in their wealth a known right, for the beggar and the deprived" (24–25)...

Here God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Except those who have in their wealth a fixed right, which is the zakah, for the beggar who asks them of their wealth, and the deprived, who has been denied wealth, so he is a poor person who does not ask."

The people of interpretation differed concerning what is meant by "the known right" mentioned by God in this passage. Some of them said: it is the zakah.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar related to me, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "And those who have in their wealth a known right, for the beggar and the deprived," he said: "The known right: the zakah."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "And those who have in their wealth a known right," he said: "The prescribed zakah."

Others said: rather, that is a right other than the zakah.

Those who said that:

'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "And those who have in their wealth a known right, for the beggar and the deprived," he said: it is other than the charity by which one keeps ties of kinship, or by which one hosts a guest, or by which one carries a burden, or by which one helps a deprived person.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Yunus, from Rabah ibn 'Ubaydah, from Qaz'ah, that Ibn 'Umar was asked concerning His words, "And those who have in their wealth a known right, for the beggar and the deprived," "Is it the zakah?" He said: "Indeed, upon you are rights other than that."

Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: Bayan related to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Indeed in wealth there is a right other than the zakah."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "In wealth there is a right other than the zakah."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mujahid: "In their wealth a known right," he said: "other than the zakah." And they agreed that the beggar is the one whose description has been given.

They also differed concerning the meaning of "the deprived" in this passage, in the same way as they differed about it in Surat al-Dhariyat. We have mentioned what they said there and indicated the sound view among them in our judgment, except that we mention some of the reports we did not mention there.

Those who said: he is the *muhtarif* [[In the lisan: the muhtarif is one who does not attain any good from any direction he turns to. Al-Shafi'i said: the deprived *muhtarif* is one who earns his living by his hands, whose share of the spoils has been cut off, who does not go out to fight with the Muslims, so he remains deprived, and what he is given from charity does not meet his need.]].

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj informed us, from al-Walid ibn al-'Aizar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The deprived: he is the *muhtarif*."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The deprived: the *muhtarif*."

Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Qays ibn Kurkum, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "*For the beggar and the deprived*: the *muhtarif* who has no share in Islam."

He says: And those who in this world are fearful of the punishment of their Lord, that He may punish them in the Hereafter; so out of fear of that they do not neglect any obligation to Him, nor transgress His limits.

* *

His words: "Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be deemed safe" (28).

Meaning: it cannot be assumed safe from befalling whoever disobeys Him and opposes His command.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 70, verses 29–31:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors﴾

Says the Exalted: ﴿And those who guard their private parts﴾, meaning: they guard their private parts from everything Allah has forbidden them to place them in, ﴿except﴾ that they are not blameworthy in leaving their guarding of them, ﴿with their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ from their female slaves. It has also been said: ﴿who guard their private parts, except with their wives﴾, without a preceding negation, because of the indication of His saying: ﴿for indeed, they are not blameworthy﴾, that the speech carries the meaning of negation. This is like the saying of the speaker: "Do whatever you wish, except for committing disobedience, for indeed you will be punished for it," meaning: "Do whatever you wish, except that you will be punished for committing disobedience."

* *

His saying: ﴿But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors﴾

So whoever seeks, for his private part, a sexual partner other than his wife or what his right hand possesses, then those who do that are the transgressors, who have exceeded what Allah made lawful for them to what He forbade them, so they are the blameworthy.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 32–39:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant, [being] custodians﴾ [32] ﴿And those who stand up in their testimonies﴾ [33] ﴿And those who maintain their prayer﴾ [34] ﴿Those will be in gardens, honored﴾ [35].

His saying, exalted is He, means: And those who are, [in relation to] the trusts of Allah which He has entrusted them with from His obligations, and the trusts of His servants which they were entrusted with, and His covenants which He took from them to obey Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, and the covenants of His servants which they gave to one another in accordance with what He has bound on Himself for them, are custodians: watching over them, guarding them, and not wasting them. Rather, they fulfill them and keep them, in accordance with what Allah has obligated them and made it binding upon them to preserve. ﴿And those who stand up in their testimonies﴾ means: those who do not conceal what they have been called to witness, but rather uphold its discharge wherever its discharge is required of them, without altering it or changing it. ﴿And those who maintain their prayer﴾ means: those who observe the appointed times of their prayers, which Allah has enjoined upon them, and its limits, which He has made obligatory for them, and who do not waste its appointed time or its limit.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Those will be in gardens, honored﴾

means: the Mighty and Majestic says: those who do these deeds are in gardens, honored, whom Allah honors with His honor.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you [O Muhammad], [30] from the right and from the left in groups?﴾ [36, 37] ﴿Does every man among them aspire to enter a garden of bliss?﴾ [38] ﴿No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know﴾ [39].

His saying, exalted is He, means: What is the matter with those who disbelieve in Allah before you, O Muhammad, hastening [muhti'een]? We have already explained the meaning of al-Ihtta' (hastening) and what the people of interpretation said about it in the past, which suffices so as not to repeat it here, except that we mention in this place some of what we did not mention there.

Qatadah said concerning it:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya reported to us, saying: Bishr reported to us, saying: Yazid reported to us, saying: Sa'id reported to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you, hastening﴾: he said: "intending" (ʿāmidīn).

Ibn Zayd said concerning it:

Yunus reported to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you, hastening﴾: he said: "al-Muhti' is the one who does not blink." Some of the knowledgeable people of the Arabic language from Basra used to say: its meaning is "hastening" (musri'een).

It is narrated concerning it from al-Hasan:

Ibn Bashshar reported to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir reported to us, saying: Qurrah reported to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you, hastening﴾: he said: "going forth" (munṭaliqīn).

Ibn Bashshar reported to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah reported to us, saying: Qurrah reported to us, from al-Hasan, the same.

* *

And His saying: ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾

means: from your right, O Muhammad, and from your left, dispersed into circles and assemblies, group by group, turning away from you and from the Book of Allah.

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd reported to me, saying: my father reported to me, saying: my paternal uncle reported to me, saying: my father reported to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you, hastening﴾: he said: "[They are] looking at you," ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾: he said: "al-ʿIzīn are the clusters (al-ʿiṣab) of people from the right and the left, turning away from him, mocking him."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr reported to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim reported to us, saying: ʿĪsa reported to us; and al-Harith reported to me, saying: al-Hasan reported to us, saying: Warqa' reported to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾: he said: "assemblies, flanking."

Bishr reported to us, saying: Yazid reported to us, saying: Sa'id reported to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you, hastening﴾: he said: "intending," ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾: i.e., scattered groups around the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, not desiring the Book of Allah nor His Prophet.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla reported to us, saying: Ibn Thawr reported to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿ʿIzīn﴾: he said: "al-ʿIzīn: circles, assemblies."

ʿAn al-Husayn reported to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd reported to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿ʿIzīn﴾: he said: "circles and companions."

Yunus reported to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾: he said: "The assembly in which there are three or four, and the assemblies of three or four, those are the ʿIzūn."

Ismaʿil ibn Musa al-Fazari reported to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas informed us, from ʿAsim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, raising it [to the Prophet ﷺ], he said: "Mā lī arākum ʿizīn" (What is [the matter] with you that I see you in groups?), and al-ʿIzīn are the scattered circles.

Ibn Bashshar reported to us, saying: Mu'mil reported to us, saying: Shaqiq reported to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ went out to his companions while they were in circles, circles, and said: "Mā lī arākum ʿizīn."

Abu Husayn reported to me, saying: ʿAbthar reported to us, saying: al-Aʿmash reported to us, from al-Musayyib ibn Rafiʿ, from Tamim ibn Tarafah al-Ta'i, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in upon us while we were dispersed, and he said: "Mā lakum ʿizīn."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr al-Ghazzi reported to me, saying: al-Firyabi reported to us, saying: Sufyan reported to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Musayyib ibn Rafiʿ, from Tamim ibn Tarafah, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ came to some of his companions while they were sitting, and he said: "Mā lī arākum ʿizīn ḥilqā" (What is [the matter] with you that I see you in circles?).

Ibn Humayd reported to us, saying: Mihran reported to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Musayyib ibn Rafiʿ, from Tamim ibn Tarafah, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ came to some of his companions while they were sitting, and he said: "Mā lī arākum ʿizīn ḥilqā."

Ibn Humayd reported to me, saying: Mihran reported to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Musayyib ibn Rafiʿ, from Tamim ibn Tarafah al-Ta'i, who said: Jabir ibn Samurah reported to us that the Prophet ﷺ went out to them while they were in circles, and he said: "Mā lī arākum ʿizīn," meaning: circles, i.e., His saying: ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾.

Ibn Bashshar reported to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir reported to us, saying: Qurrah reported to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿from the right and from the left in groups﴾: he said: "ʿIzīn: dispersed, taking right and left, saying: 'This man has not said [anything].'"

Ibn Bashshar reported to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah reported to us, saying: Qurrah reported to us, from al-Hasan, the same. The singular of ʿIzīn is ʿizah, just as the singular of thubīn is thubah, and the singular of kurīn is kurah. From the use of ʿIzīn is the saying of the camel herder:

"O Caliph of the Merciful, indeed my clan, their cattle have become ʿizīn and fulūl."[[This verse is by ʿUbayd al-Rāʿī, from a qasida of 89 verses in which he praises ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan and complains of the tax collectors (al-sussāt), who are those who collect zakat on behalf of the ruler (Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra by al-Baghdadi 1:502). The author of Jamharat Ash'ar al-ʿArab counts it among the long qasidas (pp. 172–176). Al-sawā'im: camels sent out to graze. ʿIzīn: plural of ʿizah, meaning a small group. Al-fulūl: plural of fall, meaning the remnant of a great thing, as in "the remnants of the battle lines" (fulūl al-maʿārik), i.e., the routed. He says: the tax collectors have left us only what is of no good, and have seized from us our most noble property, so there remain to us only a few scattered things here and there in our pastures, whereas before they were many. The verse is among the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 180), where he says: ʿIzīn: plural of ʿizah, like thubah and thubīn, and they are scattered groups. The Rāʿī said..." the verse. And in Fath al-Qadir by al-Shawkani (5:285), "wa-amsā sarāhum" appears in place of "amsā sawā'imuhum." The meaning on this reading is that the nobles of the poet's people came to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan group after group to complain of the oppression of the tax collectors against them. This is clear and good.]]

And His saying: ﴿Does every man among them aspire to enter a garden of bliss?﴾

means: Does every man among these disbelievers who hasten toward you, O Muhammad, hope that Allah will admit him into a garden of bliss, i.e., gardens of bliss in which he is given comfort.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿that he enter a garden of bliss﴾. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it as ﴿yudkhal﴾ with a dammah on the yā', in the passive form, except al-Hasan and Talhah ibn Musarrif, from whom it is reported that they used to recite it with a fatha on the yā', meaning: Does every man among them aspire that every man among them enter a garden of bliss.

The correct recitation in this regard is what the readers of the major cities hold, namely the dammah on the yā', due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know﴾

means: the Mighty and Majestic says: The matter is not as these disbelievers hope, that every man among them should enter a garden of bliss.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have created them from that which they know﴾

means: May He be exalted and glorified: We created them from a filthy drop of semen, and entry into Paradise is only merited by one who merits it through obedience, not by mere creation. How, then, do they aspire to enter Paradise while they are disobedient disbelievers?

And His saying: ﴿Does every man among them aspire to enter a garden of bliss?﴾

means: Does every man among these disbelievers who hasten toward you, O Muhammad, hope that Allah will admit him into a garden of bliss, i.e., gardens of bliss in which he is given comfort.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿that he enter a garden of bliss﴾. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it as ﴿yudkhal﴾ with a dammah on the yā', in the passive form, except al-Hasan and Talhah ibn Musarrif, from whom it is reported that they used to recite it with a fatha on the yā', meaning: Does every man among them aspire that every man among them enter a garden of bliss.

The correct recitation in this regard is what the readers of the major cities hold, namely the dammah on the yā', due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know﴾

means: the Mighty and Majestic says: The matter is not as these disbelievers hope, that every man among them should enter a garden of bliss.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have created them from that which they know﴾

means: May He be exalted and glorified: We created them from a filthy drop of semen, and entry into Paradise is only merited by one who merits it through obedience, not by mere creation. How, then, do they aspire to enter Paradise while they are disobedient disbelievers?

⁕ Bishr reported to us, saying: Yazid reported to us, saying: Sa'id reported to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have created them from that which they know﴾: "You were created from filth, O son of Adam, so fear Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 32–39:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant, [being] custodians﴾ [32] ﴿And those who stand up in their testimonies﴾ [33] ﴿And those who maintain their prayer﴾ [34] ﴿Those will be in gardens, honored﴾ [35].

His saying, exalted is He, means: And those who are, [in relation to] the trusts of Allah which He has entrusted them with from His obligations, and the trusts of His servants which they were entrusted with, and His covenants which He took from them to obey Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, and the covenants of His servants which they gave to one another in accordance with what He has bound on Himself for them, are custodians: watching over them, guarding them, and not wasting them. Rather, they fulfill them and keep them, in accordance with what Allah has obligated them and made it binding upon them to preserve. ﴿And those who stand up in their testimonies﴾ means: those who do not conceal what they have been called to witness, but rather uphold its discharge wherever its discharge is required of them, without altering it or changing it. ﴿And those who maintain their prayer﴾ means: those who observe the appointed times of their prayers, which Allah has enjoined upon them, and its limits, which He has made obligatory for them, and who do not waste its appointed time or its limit.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Those will be in gardens, honored﴾

means: the Mighty and Majestic says: those who do these deeds are in gardens, honored, whom Allah honors with His honor.

Yunus reported to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, racing toward you, hastening﴾: he said: "al-Muhti' is the one who does not blink." Some of the knowledgeable people of the Arabic language from Basra used to say: its meaning is "hastening" (musri'een).

Ibn Bashshar reported to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah reported to us, saying: Qurrah reported to us, from al-Hasan, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 70, verses 40–42:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So I swear not by the Lord of the easts and the wests, that We are able [to bring about] that We replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone.﴾ [40–41] ﴿So leave them to plunge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ [42]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "So I swear not by the Lord of the easts and wests of the earth" — ﴿Indeed, We are able to replace them with better than them﴾ means: Indeed, We are able to destroy them and bring in better creatures than them, who obey Me and do not disobey Me. ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾ means: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: none of them escapes Us by a matter We intend for them, so that they overpower Us by fleeing.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, he said: 'Ammarah ibn Abi Hafsah informed us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Indeed, the sun rises every year through three hundred and sixty openings (kuwwah), rising each day through one opening, and it does not return to that opening until that same day of the following year. It rises only while it is unwilling, saying: 'My Lord, do not make me rise upon Your servants, for I see them disobeying You, working at Your disobedience, I see them.'" He said: "Have you not heard the words of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt:

*until it is dragged and whipped* [[This is part of a verse by Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi:

(Al-Shi'r wa al-shu'ara' by Ibn Qutaybah, Leiden, 280). The full verse as narrated there: "She does not rise upon them in her course / except tormented, and except whipped."

He said: they say that when the sun sets, it refrains from rising, and says: "I will not rise upon a people who worship me besides Allah," until it is pushed and whipped, and so it rises.

The version of the verse in al-Aghani of Abu al-Faraj (Dar al-Kutub edition, 4:130), together with the verse before it, is: "The sun rises every last night / red, the color of its rising is reddish. / It refuses, so it does not appear to us in its course / except tormented, and except whipped."

From these two narrations it is known that the author's witness is truncated and distorted. I say: what Ibn 'Abbas said in explaining the sun's rising every year through 360 openings, etc., is correct from the standpoint of knowledge. As for the explanation of Umayyah's verse — that the angels push it until it rises, and it refuses and is whipped — it is imagery, figurative speech, and a rebuke to those who worship the sun.]]
