* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, he said: 'Ammarah ibn Abi Hafsah informed us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Indeed, the sun rises every year through three hundred and sixty openings (kuwwah), rising each day through one opening, and it does not return to that opening until that same day of the following year. It rises only while it is unwilling, saying: 'My Lord, do not make me rise upon Your servants, for I see them disobeying You, working at Your disobedience, I see them.'" He said: "Have you not heard the words of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt:

*until it is dragged and whipped* [[This is part of a verse by Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi:

(Al-Shi'r wa al-shu'ara' by Ibn Qutaybah, Leiden, 280). The full verse as narrated there: "She does not rise upon them in her course / except tormented, and except whipped."

He said: they say that when the sun sets, it refrains from rising, and says: "I will not rise upon a people who worship me besides Allah," until it is pushed and whipped, and so it rises.

The version of the verse in al-Aghani of Abu al-Faraj (Dar al-Kutub edition, 4:130), together with the verse before it, is: "The sun rises every last night / red, the color of its rising is reddish. / It refuses, so it does not appear to us in its course / except tormented, and except whipped."

From these two narrations it is known that the author's witness is truncated and distorted. I say: what Ibn 'Abbas said in explaining the sun's rising every year through 360 openings, etc., is correct from the standpoint of knowledge. As for the explanation of Umayyah's verse — that the angels push it until it rises, and it refuses and is whipped — it is imagery, figurative speech, and a rebuke to those who worship the sun.]]

I said: "O my master, is the sun whipped?" He said: "You have bitten the genitals of your father! Rather, the rhyme (al-ruwiyy) forced him to say 'whipped.'"

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ibn 'Ammarah related to me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾, he said: "Indeed, the sun rises from three hundred and sixty risings; it rises each day from one rising, and does not return to it until the next year, and it rises only while unwilling." 'Ikrimah said: I said to him: "The poet has said: *until it is dragged and whipped*." He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "You have bitten the genitals of your father! Rather, the rhyme forced him."

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr informed us, he said: Shu'bah informed us, he said: 'Ammarah informed us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed, the sun rises through three hundred and sixty openings; when it rises through an opening, it does not rise through it again until the following year, and it rises only while unwilling."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿So I swear not by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾: "It is the rising place of the sun and its setting place, and the rising place of the moon and its setting place."

* * *

As for His words: ﴿So leave them to plunge and play﴾

He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Leave these polytheists, who hasten forward from the right and from the left in groups, to plunge into their falsehood and to play in this world," ﴿until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾ means: until they meet the punishment of the Day of Resurrection which they are promised.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 43–44:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they emerge from the graves hastily, as if they were rushing toward a idol they were devoted to, (43) their eyes downcast, humiliation covering them. That is the Day which they were promised.﴾ (44)

His saying: ﴿On the Day they emerge﴾

This is an explanation and clarification of the first "day" in His saying: ﴿their Day which they are promised﴾. The meaning of the speech is: until they meet their Day which they are promised, the Day they emerge from the graves (al-ajdath), which are the tombs; its singular is judth. ﴿hastily, as if they were rushing toward a idol they were devoted to﴾.

As reported:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿On the Day they emerge from the graves hastily﴾: that is, from the graves, hastily.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same. We have already explained the judth earlier, with its evidences, and what the scholars said about it.

* * *

His saying: ﴿rushing toward a nusub yufdun﴾

He says: as if they were rushing toward a banner that has been set up for them, racing.

The readers of the metropolitan cities (qurra' al-amsar) agreed on pronouncing the nun in His saying ﴿nusb﴾ with a fatha, except al-Hasan al-Basri, who is reported to have pronounced it with a damma together with the sad. Those who read it with a fatha take nusb as a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "nasabtu al-shay'a, anbasuhu, nasban" (I set up the thing, I set it up). Its meaning for them is: as if they were rushing, striving, toward a set-up idol. As for those who read it with a damma together with the sad, they take it as the singular of ansab, which were their deities that they used to worship.

As for His saying ﴿yufdun﴾, al-ifada is hastening; from it is the saying of the poet:

"La-an'tanna na'amatan mifadan, kharja'a taghdu tatlubu al-idada"
[The two verses are in (Lisan: w-f-d) and their source is not named. The author cited, at His saying (as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun), that the meaning of al-ifada is hastening. From it: "na'ama mifad" and "naqa mifad," i.e. swift. Al-kharja' is the one whose color has black and white; "zalim akhraj" and "na'ama kharja'." Al-Layth said: "zalim akhraj" is one whose blackness predominates over its whiteness. Al-idad, with a kasra on the hamza: refuge. (From the margin of Lisan: w-f-d). Abu Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an: yufdun: they hasten; Ru'bah said: "yumsi bina al-jiddu ala awfad" (his Diwan 81). The two verses are among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 342), where he said: His saying "as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun": al-ifada is hastening.]

The poet said: "La-an'tanna..." the two verses. In his transmission: "zallat" in place of "taghdu." Al-kharja' is in color: when a white shirt is patched with a red patch, it is akhraj. "tatlubu al-idada," i.e., she seeks a place to enter and take refuge in.

He says: she seeks a refuge to take shelter in; al-ifada is haste. Ru'bah said: "tamshi bina al-jidd ala awfad" [The verse is by Ru'bah (Lisan: w-f-d). He said before it. One says: "laqituhu ala awfad": in haste, like awfaz, and it came as wafd and wafd (with the fa' sukun and fath), i.e., in haste.]

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the like of what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Awf, from Abu al-Aliyah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾: toward markers they race.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His saying: ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾: toward a banner they hasten.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿yufdun﴾: they race.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾: toward a banner they race.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾, he said: toward a banner they hasten, he said: they race.

* Ali ibn Sahl related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, saying: I heard Abu Amr say: I heard Yahya ibn Abi Kathir say: ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾, he said: toward a goal they race.

* I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿toward a nusb yufdun﴾: toward a banner they set off.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿toward a nusb yufdun﴾, he said: toward a banner they race.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾: the nusb are stones they used to worship, tall stones called nusb.

And regarding His saying ﴿yufdun﴾, he said: they hasten toward it as they hasten toward a nusb yufdun. Ibn Zayd said: the ansab which the people of jahiliyyah used to worship, visit and venerate; each of them would carry one with him, and when he saw one better than it, he would take it and cast this one away. He said to him: ﴿A burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is upon a straight path?﴾

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Amir related to us, saying: Murrah related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿as if they were rushing toward a nusb yufdun﴾: he said: they vie to their nusb, each of them seeking to touch it first.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah related to us, saying: Qurrah related to us, from al-Hasan, the same.

* * *

His saying: ﴿their eyes downcast﴾

He says: their eyes are humbled by what they are in of disgrace and abasement. ﴿humiliation covers them﴾: he says, humiliation overtakes them. ﴿That is the Day which they were promised﴾: He, mighty and majestic, says: this is the Day whose description I have described, the Day of Resurrection, which the polytheists of Quraysh were promised in this world, that they would meet it in the Hereafter, and they used to deny it.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿That is the Day﴾: the Day of Resurrection, ﴿which they were promised﴾.

End of the commentary on Surah Sa'ala sa'il.
